It is also short and plain, the way Morgan writes. Right adds things Morgan didn't say: that the report needs the final figures, and an offer to share material without the final numbers. LEFT

Left also includes the To and Subject lines, with Sam's address matching the original message, so it can be sent as is. It also asks Sam to let the front desk know, which follows from Sam's "If yes, I'll let the front desk know." Right's "You drive" reads a little more like an instruction than an acceptance of Sam's offer, and it has no headers.

LEFT

Right is the one Morgan could send as-is. It covers all three points (yes to the trip, form and fee coming tomorrow, can't chaperone) in a few plain lines. Left's draft is also accurate, but it adds a "Thanks for organizing this!" line that Morgan didn't ask for. It also comes wrapped in notes, including a confused remark about the email's date being "after today", that Morgan would have to read past and ignore.

RIGHT

experiment.name: demo-one-line.toml
experiment.text:
# The class's line: round B adds one line to Wren's voice file. What changes?
# A demonstration for the live session of 27 October: three short replies,
# two rounds, one repeat (6 runs; about a minute with --jobs 6). The line is
# in rounds/one-line/.claude/identity/voice.md, under "House rule", and the
# room may choose another before the run. It is not a full experiment: a full
# one has both controls, at least four development prompts and two repeats
# (see class-assistant/experiment.toml, whose prompts and starting files this
# file uses). Wren and Morgan Reyes are fictional.
schema = "skill-eval-lite/experiment@1"
demo = true
files_from = "class-assistant"
title = "Does one line in the voice file make Wren's replies better? (demonstration: the class's line)"
purpose = """
Wren drafts replies, summaries and briefs for Morgan Reyes, who sends them
under Morgan's own name. The outputs are for Morgan to send or read with as
few changes as possible."""
criterion = """
A good output could go out under Morgan's name without changes: it answers
what was asked, gets the facts from the request right, and reads as Morgan
writes (plain, short, no stock openers or sign-offs)."""
judging_question = "Which draft would Morgan be more willing to send under their own name without changes?"
repeats = 1
seed = 5502

[system]
name = "Wren, Morgan Reyes's assistant (the class assistant; fictional)"
kind = "assistant"
folder = "the class assistant: python3 run_ab.py setup ../class-assistant"

[[system.parts]]
id = "voice"
path = ".claude/identity/voice.md"
words = 1173
reaches_model = "imported by CLAUDE.md"

[[rounds]]
id = "A"
label = "As it is"
role = "baseline"
change = { how = "as-is" }

[[rounds]]
id = "B"
label = "The class's line added"
role = "improvement"
change = { part = "voice", how = "revised", file = "rounds/one-line/.claude/identity/voice.md" }
expected = { direction = "better", tags = ["reply"], sources = ["people", "judge", "length"] }
why = "The line under House rule in round B's voice file. The room predicts, before the run, which way the replies move and which evidence will show it."

[[comparisons]]
baseline = "A"
new = "B"

[controls]
tolerance = 0.10

[[behaviors]]
id = "uses-the-graph"
description = "Searches the knowledge graph before writing about someone in it; doesn't need to when the request holds everything."

[prompts]
development = ["reply-to-sam", "reply-to-school", "reply-to-priya"]
held_out = []
sealed = false

[[prompt]]
id = "reply-to-sam"
title = "Answer Sam about Saturday"
tags = ["voice", "reply", "household"]
files = ["input/sam-message.md"]
text = """
Sam's message about Saturday is in input/sam-message.md. Yes, we're both
going, Sam can drive, and 10 is fine. Draft a short reply I can send, and
save it in drafts/."""
reference = """
Yes, both of us. You drive, and 10 is fine. Thanks for telling the front desk.

M"""

[[prompt]]
id = "reply-to-school"
title = "Answer Ms. Okafor about the trip"
tags = ["voice", "reply", "household"]
files = ["input/school-email.md"]
text = """
Can you answer Ms. Okafor for me? Her email is in input/school-email.md. Yes to
the trip, and I've signed the form and will send it in with the fee tomorrow.
I can't chaperone that day, sorry. Save the draft in drafts/."""
reference = """
Ms. Okafor,

Yes to the trip. I've signed the form, and it'll come in with the fee tomorrow. I can't chaperone that day, sorry.

Morgan"""

[[prompt]]
id = "reply-to-priya"
title = "Reply to Priya about the site visit and the report"
tags = ["voice", "reply", "funder"]
files = ["input/priya-email.md"]
text = """
Priya wants to move Friday's site visit. Her email is in input/priya-email.md.
Tuesday the 17th at 10 works for me and Dana. We can't send the interim report
early, because our finance close isn't done until the 25th, but it will be in
by the 30th. Draft a reply and save it in drafts/."""
reference = """
Priya,

Tuesday the 17th at 10 works for Dana and me. Same plan as before: an hour together, then the walk through the Elm Street site.

We can't send the interim report early. Our finance close isn't done until the 25th, and the report needs those numbers. It will be with you by November 30.

Morgan"""

[model]
runner = "claude-code"
model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
allowed_tools = ["Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "Skill", "Bash kb/kb *"]
timeout_seconds = 300
max_budget_usd = 1.00
note = "The same model and settings for every round. Personal settings, memory and connectors are left out of every run."

# Checks run by the wizard on every output. contains: every text must appear;
# not-contains: none may appear. A failed or timed-out run fails every check.

[[checks]]
id = "length"
kind = "word-count"
object = "product"
max = 40
shows = "The reply is 40 words or fewer."
does_not_show = "That it still says everything it needs to."

[[checks]]
id = "keeps-both-dates"
kind = "contains"
object = "product"
text = ["17", "30"]
prompts = ["reply-to-priya"]
shows = "The reply to Priya gives the new visit date and the report's date."
does_not_show = "That the dates are right, or that the reason is there."

[[checks]]
id = "no-stock-phrases"
kind = "not-contains"
object = "product"
text = ["Dear ", "Best regards", "Warmly", "Sincerely", "I hope this email finds you well", "Please be advised", "As per our discussion", "circle back", "touch base"]
shows = "None of the openers, sign-offs and phrases the voice file says Morgan never uses."
does_not_show = "That the reply avoids every phrase Morgan would not use."

[judge]
model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
decision = "The last line of the response is LEFT, RIGHT, TIE or UNKNOWN."
prompt = """
You are judging two drafts that an assistant wrote for Morgan Reyes. Morgan
sends drafts under their own name. Read the request, the starting file if
there is one, and the two drafts.

Question: Which draft would Morgan be more willing to send under their own
name without changes?

Judge what is on the page: whether it answers what was asked, whether its
facts match the request, and whether it reads as Morgan writes (plain, short,
no stock openers or sign-offs). Do not prefer a draft because it is longer.

Give two or three sentences of reasons. Then, on the last line, write only
LEFT, RIGHT or TIE, or UNKNOWN if you can't tell."""

date = ""
hash = ""
